posts.cooked:
I registered just to kvetch, and fortuitously enough, I saw that a thread already existed for just that purpose.

Tempest, Visionary, Tachyon, and Absolute Zero vs. Citizen Dawn in Megalopolis. The initial citizen draw is relatively unremarkable, but it does contain Citizen Tears. Okay, no big. Dawn hits her play phase and flips "Blinding Blast". Huh, okay, nobody's had a turn yet and we're already down to just one card in our hand. We can't finish off Tears on the first go-'round, but Tempest gets out an electrical storm and Zero gets out a cold snap, so it's just a matter of time. We flip the environment card and... Traffic Pileup. Well, that's annoying. Dawn gets her turn, which is unremarkable except for the fact that Citizen Tears takes care of the last card in everyone's hand. Our heroes all go again and can't do anything during the play or draw phases, but at least between the Start of Turn effects and Tempest's innate power, we manage to finish off Tears and start whittling down that Traffic Pileup. Then we get to the environment turn. We flip the top card and... Paparazzi on the Scene. Well crap- now we have no play phase, no power phase, no draw phase, and no way to do anything until our Start of Turn effects finally finish off that Traffic Pileup. I think to myself "wow, this has to be the lamest game imagineable". 

Then, after we get Traffic Pileup down to 1 HP, Dawn flips Devastating Aurora. No cards in our hands, no cards on the table, everyone under half health, Dawn at 70+ health and two citizens from flipping.

I would like to say that I chose the heroic path, that I played it out. I would like to say that I managed to hang around, eking out a hard-won victory or a hard-fought defeat. I would like to say that I did not simply flip the table and ragequit. I would like to say that.

Edit: Honestly, the Aurora helped us, because it saved us a turn getting rid of the Paparrazi on the scene, and toasting Cold Snap and Electrical Storm gave us more control over when she flipped. It was just the general sense of "what now". Typically Sentinels is a very fun game, but there was absolutely nothing fun for anyone involved in that one.

I can enjoy being on the receiving end of a well-deserved beatdown as much as the next guy. Lord knows I probably deserve a few more just to even the score (the first time I encountered Self Destruct Sequence basically went like this: 1) Read card. 2) "Kind of annoying..." 3) Look at Haka's hand. 4) Read Ground Pound. 5) Laugh maniacally.) With that said, some cards negatively impact my fun whether I'm winning or losing. On a meta level, Sentinels is all about the choices we make and the actions we prioritize in our quest to outrace the game mechanics. On a thematic level, Sentinels is all about getting an opportunity to be larger than life, wielding superhuman power. Anything that prevents us from making choices or wielding power is a nuisance. One or two nuisance cards isn't a big deal, and in fact makes for a more interesting game as we struggle to overcome our handicaps. Three or four nuisance cards, and Sentinels basically devolves into a very pretty, colorful version of the card game War. It's not that I'm losing, or even that all of my efforts are futile, it's that I'm unable to make an effort at all. I basically have to just sit around and wait for a deus ex machina.

Thankfully, games like that one are an aberration. And perhaps that will be the last time I take on a villian who can force discards in an environment like Megalopolis where nearly half the deck (7/15 cards) depends on the players having spare cards to discard.

Last night I bought the Rook City expansion pack, and we were playing it blind with four friends; that is, we didn’t have time to look at decks before playing them, so we had no idea what Spite could do until he did it. He was beating the everloving Christ out of us, because the first card he got out was the drug card that makes the players remove (H-2) ongoing and/or equipment cards from play. Since our team was Tempest, Omnitron-X, the Wraith, Mr. Fixer, and Absolute Zero, we all had to sacrifice a lot just to get Wraith and Zero playable, and he was inflicting so much damage that he was vampired back up to full HP at the end of his every turn.

The very last card in his deck is his final drug card, so he finally, finally flips. All of us are in the low teens for HP and he’s still at full health, but at least he’s not regenerating from every blow he lands. Everyone is afraid to hurt him because all their damage effects rely on powers, and he’s going to counter each power.

I’m playing Mr. Fixer and I get the grease gun card; you know, the equipment card that leaves Mr. Fixer unable to use powers or draw cards, but prevents non-heroes from doing damage and is destroyed at the beginning of his turn. I play it, and his drug cards have me returning the grease gun to my hand at the end of his turn so I can just play it again to screw him out of being able to inflict damage.

He’s still at eighty HP, but we all decide to end the game there because he’s functionally incapable of inflicting damage on us any more, and the only thing left to do is to just wait and see how long it takes us to chip him down to zero. Victory was assured, but only at a snail’s pace.

Winning badly is worse than losing well, I think.

It's good having Mr Fixer against Spite actually, because as long as the environment doesn't hit you on its turn, you can keep playing Bloody Knuckles and punch Spite for extra damage, have him put it back into your hand before hitting you (so no +2 damage dealt to you), then play it again on your turn :D. This also means you can actually deal damage to Spite with your base power without needing to use a damaging one-shot or a damage-boosting tool or style (or Tiger Claw) to be able to deal him damage once he has his soak-damage-from-the-first-hit-every-turn card out.

Wraith does well at double-Stun-Bolting him once she gets set up with those and a Utility Belt, causing him to do sod all damage to everyone else (and none to Wraith either if she has Smoke Bombs out and the lowest hp), plus she's capable of getting set up quite nicely if she can get hold of even one copy of Impromptu Invention. Omni-10, similarly, can keep Timeshifting himself to get as many components out as he can, with the EDUs accelerating his set-up significantly. Temporal Shielding is probably the best plating to have out since Demon's Kiss deals infernal damage while Mind Phyre is psychic. The get-hit-and-discard-when-you-use-a-power is toxic, but if you're pretty well set up by then you can get away with not using any powers and still kick his arse. Having a Plasma Cannon out before the Gaussian Coil thingy means you get to burn through his soak and cause him to waste it on your irreducible damage before the non-irreducible lightning damage hits. Even if you keep using powers after the toxic damage drug comes out, with two Innervation Rays you can heal back the damage (or most of it, once Spite has the damage-boosting drug out) every turn. Also, now I think of it, Omni-10 is probably a good candidate to lose a card back to hand from the drug that does that, because he can just replay it via an EDU in his Start phase and still play something else in his Play phase :).

It is annoying, though, if Spite gets out the more annoying drugs first - we tend to find the toxic-damage-and-discard one is the worst, unless we can nerf his damage enough (which usually happens when I'm playing Wraith ;)) to make it less punishing to use powers - the discard isn't so bad unless you're trying to organise your deck a certain way to get hold of cards (like Visionary or Adept putting certain cards to the top of their decks), and Tachyon probably has an advantage in it, as long as she doesn't burn right through her deck to the reshuffle point before having a chance to do a multi-Lightspeed Barrage whammy.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Vengeance style in Realm of Discord.  Using the Converted Apostate from BGG, with Fright Train, Friction and Blade.

First environment turn:  Time Flies (seriously ouch, we got the worst cards from the villains)

Second Environment Turn:  Clausterphobic Delusions  (Yeah, so Apostate had a ton of relics in play, so lowest HP target was Periapt of Woe, Runes of Melediction were in play.  So the only target not immune was at -4 damage taken.)

 

Third environment turn was awesome:  Ghostly images, we did Adept first, and he played Vernal Sonata, letting everyone put a one-shot on top before Ghostly hit them, that was awesome.  But still too little when that one nemesis is increasing your damage taken by one, and you can't damage anything but a -4 taken relic.

 

We had Adept, Ra, Fixer and Bunker, so until adept got his destruction we were stuck with Clausterphobic, which lasted till round 6.

We had destroyed periapt, but Malediction and corrupted Effigy were giving us fits.  We ended up living long enough to take out Friction, but it was a terrible game.  I forgot the Apostate/Clausterphobic shenanigans, but honestly, getting a perfect storm like that isn't likely, esp. going three rounds without being able to destroy a distortion.
